findings.claim: Debug logging left in at Error level in the cleanup closures (lines 534/537/554/557/576/579): every batch, including successful and empty ones, emits two r.log.Error lines, the first dumping the full ids slice (up to cleanupjob_batchsize entries) plus cond, and 'err' is always nil on the first line.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'r.log.Error' xorm_store.go shows 6 new call sites; untilDoneOrCancelled needs a 0-row batch to stop so an idle run still logs ~14 Error lines. Breaches contribute/backend/instrumentation.md: Error level is for unhandled failures; messages must start with a capital letter and use key 'error' not 'err' (537/557/579 lowercase). Reasoned; no test run.
findings.reason: Unanimous across seats; production log noise and error-alert false positives, plus documented-standard breach. Remove or demote to Debug with count only.

findings.claim: Global cleanup ticker changed from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1, running all cleanup jobs (tmp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x as often; unrelated to the annotation fix and looks like a debugging leftover.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk at cleanup.go:77; per-run timeout at cleanup.go:89 is still 9*time.Minute, sized for a 10-minute cadence, so slow runs go back-to-back. No commit message justifies it. Increases DB load/lock contention on a PR meant to reduce it. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Unanimous; out-of-scope behaviour change affecting every install. Revert to time.Minute*10.

findings.claim: SQLite inline-ID path builds the IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop, which is quadratic in batch size.
findings.evidence: At batch size 32767 (used by the new test) the final string is ~200-230KB and total copying is several GB per batch. Reasoned, not measured. Only on SQLite with batch size > 999.
findings.reason: Cheap fix (strconv.AppendInt into one buffer, as xorm_store.go:387-395 already does); resolved by the single-path rewrite below.

findings.claim: Non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID with no cap; MySQL and Postgres reject statements with more than 65535 bind parameters, so cleanupjob_batchsize > 65535 makes every DELETE fail, a regression from the old parameterless subquery.
findings.evidence: deleteByIDs else-branch uses asAny(ids) as args; default batch size is 100 (pkg/setting/setting.go:710), so only extreme configs hit it. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Eliminated by inlining int64 IDs on all dialects (single-path rewrite); otherwise would be defer as non-default config. Inlined path still bounded by SQLITE_MAX_SQL_LENGTH (~140k ids) - acceptable.

findings.claim: Comment states 'SQLite has a parameter limit of 999', which is only true before SQLite 3.32 (32766 after); the new test name references the 3.32 limit, so the comment is misleading. Branch also gates on configured batch size rather than len(ids).
findings.evidence: xorm_store.go:605-608 vs test case name in cleanup_test.go. No behavioural bug.
findings.reason: Goes away with the single-path rewrite; otherwise a one-line comment correction.

findings.claim: Two SQL paths in deleteByIDs (inlined for SQLite>999, placeholders elsewhere) where one suffices: IDs are int64 read back from the DB, so inlining them is injection-safe, and the same file already inlines integer IDs on every dialect. Collapsing removes the GetDBType branch, sqliteParameterLimit, args, asAny and the migrator import (~20 lines).
findings.evidence: Existing precedent at xorm_store.go:387-395 (dashboard_id IN built with strconv.AppendInt); asAny at :632. Advisory over-engineering finding; all seats agree inlining int64s is not an injection risk.
findings.reason: Advisory but accepted: one change resolves the quadratic build, the 65535-placeholder cap and the stale comment, with net code deletion.

findings.claim: The fetch->log->delete->log closure is copied three times (by time, by count, tags) with opaque x, y temporaries; copies have already drifted in log wording.
findings.reason: ponytail: once the Error logs are removed each closure collapses to ~2 lines (return r.deleteByIDs(...)); a cleanBatch helper is not needed now.

findings.claim: fetchIDs guards condition == "" although all callers pass a non-empty condition, so the guard is dead code.
findings.evidence: xorm_store.go:586-588; three callers build conditions via fmt.Sprintf always containing a predicate. Advisory.
findings.reason: The guard prevents 'SELECT id FROM table WHERE ' degenerating into a full-table selection feeding a DELETE; data-loss-preventing validation is kept even if currently unreachable. 3 lines.

findings.claim: MaxCount return was rewritten from 'return totalAffected, err' to an if-err-return plus shared return; behaviour identical, pure diff churn.
findings.reason: No behavioural or readability defect; reverting would itself be churn with zero benefit.

findings.claim: createTestAnnotations duplicates the 500-row InsertMulti chunk loop for annotations and annotation tags, and calls require.NoError inside the DB callback then returns nil.
findings.reason: ponytail: test-helper duplication of ~8 lines; not worth churn in this PR.

findings.claim: Subtest registers t.Cleanup only after createTestAnnotations and count assertions; if seeding fails via require (FailNow) the partially inserted rows are never cleaned and leak into later subtests sharing fakeSQL, masking the real failure.
findings.evidence: cleanup_test.go:116 seeds, :120 registers t.Cleanup. contribute/backend/style-guide.md 'Cleanup' recommends t.Cleanup. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Two-line move (register cleanup before seeding) makes failures diagnosable.

findings.claim: Case 'running the max count delete again should not remove any annotations' no longer runs cleanup a second time over prior state because each case now seeds fresh data; idempotency of a repeated run is no longer tested and the name is misleading.
findings.evidence: cleanup_test.go:83 plus per-subtest createTestAnnotations at :116 and t.Cleanup at :120. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Rename the case to describe what it asserts (or run cleanup twice within it).

findings.claim: Test seeding sets explicit IDs (ID: int64(i+1)); on Postgres explicit IDs do not advance annotation_id_seq, so a later test inserting via the sequence without clearing could hit duplicate keys.
findings.evidence: xorm only skips autoincrement when value is zero (pkg/util/xorm/session_insert.go:153,:204). Every subtest currently empties the table, so harmless today. Reasoned, low risk.
findings.reason: ponytail: latent only; no current test triggers it and the table is emptied after each subtest.
